body:
Received this feedback from Bart Preneel:

> Consider adding: AEGIS (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-irtf-cfrg-aegis-aead/) as it is substantially faster than all other modes.

References:

* [AEGIS: A Fast Authenticated Encryption Algorithm (v1.1)](https://competitions.cr.yp.to/round3/aegisv11.pdf)
* [The AEGIS Family of Authenticated Encryption Algorithms ](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-irtf-cfrg-aegis-aead/)
* [AEGIS: A Fast Authenticated Encryption Algorithm (Full Version)](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/695.pdf)

Note that Bart Preneel is one of the designers of AEGIS.

comments.body: AEGIS has been deployed at Google and other large organizations for a while. Besides performance, it has interesting properties that makes it less prone to foot-shooting than AES-GCM. The specification is finalized and ready to be passed to the RFC editor. AEGIS has [many implementations](https://github.com/cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-aegis-aead?tab=readme-ov-file#known-implementations) including in TLS stacks, and is the recommended AEAD in libsodium. So, it may be worth adding to ASVS.

It wouldn't hurt to add 128X and 256X. 128L and 256 are just specific instantiation of these, and they all share the same security properties.

The stream cipher and MAC constructions can be ignored; for most use cases, they are difficult to justify over existing schemes.

Some caution - it's still in draft no https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-irtf-cfrg-aegis-aead/
I do like it and I will 100% support it when it is adopted but I think, for clarities sake, we should only ensure we are adding in bits that are proven, broadly secure, and standardised algorithms. Yes, we can be forward looking and maybe this is where the appendix might be best, and why we think so, but adding it into V11 wouldn't sit well with me

All three main variants—AEGIS-128, AEGIS-128L, and AEGIS-256—are considered “stable” designs from the AEGIS family. They were all selected as finalists in the CAESAR competition for authenticated encryption and have undergone heavy-duty cryptanalysis without any critical breaks.

AEGIS-128X and AEGIS-256X are not part of the CAESAR-submitted AEGIS variants, and  they are not widely recognized or even standardized.
So there is a consensus on listing AEGIS-128, AEGIS-128L, and AEGIS-256 as approved AEADs? If so, I'll make a PR for that.
